question: A fatwa issued by the Mufti of Mostar, Salem ef. Dedović, has been used as an argument in a court case before the Municipal Court in Mostar concerning the construction of the Croatian National Theatre building. This religious edict presents claims about the legal status of the site and the legality of the construction.

Public and media reports about the case have employed photomontages and AI-generated images in which the theatre building is surrounded by human bones, skulls and bags containing supposed mortal remains, teamed with graphical representations of blood. In view of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s status as a candidate country: 1.
Is the Commission aware of this case?

Does it consider the use of religious edicts in court cases to be compatible with the EU’s fundamental values, in particular the rule of law, the independence of the judiciary and the secular nature of the institutions?

How does it intend to respond to the case and to public reports, including the use of factually unfounded and disturbing visual content liable to fuel interethnic and interfaith tensions in an election year, and will it consider this case in its reporting on Bosnia and Herzegovina’s progress?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.11.2026) The Commission closely monitors, assesses, and reports on the functioning of the judiciary of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the Commission’s Enlargement Package1 and Annual Report2, particularly under chapter 23 (Judiciary and Fundamental Rights).

The Commission does not comment on the substance of individual court cases or the merits of the legal arguments presented therein, which fall within the competence of the relevant judicial authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The Commission recalls that concerns about the conduct of online and printed media outlets can be addressed to the Press and Online Media Council of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which plays an important role in ensuring that media complies with professional standards, including by handling complaints from citizens.
